meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to add', forming an aspectual pair with 'добавлять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to append') (to say in addition) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'спорить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'lose a bet'.

examples.trans: You lost the bet. Five thousand?

examples.text: Ты же вчера при всех честно проспорил мне пять тысяч!
examples.trans: Yesterday in front of everyone you fairly lost a five-thousand-ruble bet to me!

examples.text: Сеня боялся проспорить Феде целую коробку дорогих сигар.
examples.trans: Senya was afraid of losing a whole box of expensive cigars in a bet to Fedya.

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'meeting; date' in everyday Russian.

'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Сломать руку = to break one's arm. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.
